text:
lisa: opening a thread — prototype for an edge/route packer that aggregates tiny chat requests before runtime enqueue. goal = cut p99 for sub-50-token chats.
chao: High level: router coalesces concurrent items into a packed envelope and sends one logical request to runtime. runtime still enforces admission and does KV pinning/unpack.
rachel: My main worry is queuing semantics. router could hide runtime headroom pressure and cause larger backpressure cascades. how do we surface headroom?
lisa: plan: runtime returns an advisory header `X-Headroom: low|ok` on enqueue responses. router keeps per-shard recent headroom samples; if low, router throttles packing for 500ms for that shard.
tom: Fairness concern: cross-tenant packing can improve throughput but hurts isolation. Any tenant-stealing mitigations?
lisa: yes — soft tenant credits at router plus a conservative hot-tenant fastpath. if tenant uses >50% of its soft credit in rolling 60s, router bypasses cross-tenant packing for that tenant.
priya: What about mixed-length packs? combining short and long will spike tokens/req and KV misses. can we limit heterogeneity?
chao: Router will bucket candidates by model+length_bin and only pack within same bucket. also add `prefix-sha` hint for runtime prefetch.
lisa: here's the proto config we tested:```yaml
edge_packer:
  enabled: true
  pack_window_ms: 7
  max_items: 10
  min_tokens: 6
  per_tenant_soft_credit: 200
  hot_tenant_threshold: 0.5
  length_buckets: [0-32,33-128,129-512]
  prefix_hint_len: 24
  honor_runtime_headroom_ms: 500
  small_bypass_tokens: 10
```
rachel: Observability: we need `edge.pack_rate`, `edge.pack_rejects_hot`, `edge.unpacked_sample_rate`, and traces that annotate packed->unpacked mapping. also correlate with `runtime.kv_miss_rate` and `runtime.enqueue_latency`.
tom: Rollout strategy suggestion: 10% canary per region, monitor 30m windows. auto-degrade rule: if runtime.kv_miss_rate rises >2% absolute or p99 latency increases >8% then disable in that shard.
priya: Also add a guard for tiny interactive typing flows — bypass if user-visible latency budget < 40ms. can't risk adding packing delay.
lisa: good call. router will bypass packing for requests with `interactive=true` header or tokens <= small_bypass_tokens.
chao: Another important handshake — admission credits. runtime must reject or return a special `ENQUEUE_DEFER` if it can't accept the packed envelope. router should then split and re-enqueue per-item, not drop.
rachel: For debugging: packed envelopes obscure item-level logs. add a sampled unpack trace: `edge.unpack_sample_rate=1/500` and include original request ids in span.
tom: Performance tradeoffs: earlier packing reduces runtime enqueue jitter but raises risk of mis-prefetch. prefix_hint + async prefetch should mitigate most. measure tokens_per_request and cost delta closely.
lisa: test plan: canary 10% for 1 hour with synthetic traffic mix (75% short, 25% long) + a hot tenant at 45% load. collect p50/p95/p99, tokens/req, kv_miss_rate, eviction_events/sec, tenant_throughput_skew.
priya: Eval harness: add long-doc prompts with repeated prefixes to surface cold-warmup regressions.
infra-bot: deploybot: scheduled canary on infra-canary-9 in 20m. watching metrics: edge.pack_rate, runtime.kv_miss_rate, p99_latency, tenant_throughput_skew. auto-rollback if p99 + kv_miss thresholds hit.
lisa: action items: Lisa = push PR + dashboards; Chao = runtime headroom header impl; Rachel = observability queries + alerts; Tom = canary runbook; Priya = eval prompt set.
lisa: thanks all — hoping this gives a low-risk path to better small-request latency without touching the continuous-batcher core yet. :rocket:
